operations.resource: cloudwatch:DELETES the two live replica route-freshness alarms named literally in the closure — a LOSS of observability, not an addition. It selects them by exact AlarmName, never by prefix, because a prefix that matches nothing makes a destructive delete succeed while changing nothing. apply gates on four facts and aborts unless all hold: the edge-read-from-replica parameter is readable and not true, the replication group's members are enumerable, the ASG reports at least one InService edge (and any supplied instance list matches that set exactly), and EVERY InService edge reports over SSM that its effective reader host equals its primary. It saves each alarm's full live definition under this run's id before deleting, asserts the delete readback, and rollback recreates them from that run's file and compares the restored properties and dimensions.

iam:EdgeRole cloudwatch:PutMetricData restricted to namespace OpenClaw/Edge. FAIL-CLOSED PREREQUISITE. apply first asserts the shipped policy document matches the statement the closure adds, then applies it only if the effective decision is not already allowed, then asserts the decision. The same check is exposed as a `gate` mode, which s3-edge-bundle apply calls before it uploads and which APPLY runs before replacing files on running edge hosts, so the ordering is enforced by the tool rather than by document order. rollback is a deliberate no-op that exits 0 with the reason: removing the grant makes the metric permanently absent, which is indistinguishable from an unapplied kit.

s3:assets edge bundle prefix AND the cr-owned bucket tag that tracks it. The prefix is read from the closure, never guessed. apply calls the IAM gate first, uploads, then downloads every shipped object back and compares its sha256 to the shipped bytes, then swaps the cr-owned tag and asserts the new tag is present. rollback restores the recorded tag set and explains that removing the objects is only safe once no Launch Template version references the prefix.

s3:observability asset deployments (the fluent-bit installer and the edge/host configs). Root cause is content change under deploy/edge/fluent-bit/ in this range, not a change to observability.py, which is outside it. apply records each object's current version id, uploads, then downloads every object back and compares its sha256 to the shipped bytes; rollback prints those version ids, because this bucket is versioned.

s3:deployment/bootstrap/host/<sha256>/init-host.sh AND the Host Launch Template version the ASG pins. MANUAL by design: the prefix IS the sha256 of the RENDERED script (ha_edge.py computes `_init_sha256 = sha256(init_sh)`), so the closure's digest was produced from config.yml.example and is NOT this environment's expected value — it can only be COMPUTED from the script this fleet actually serves. `plan` does that computation read-only: it reads the digest the ASG-pinned LT requests, downloads that object, asserts the object's own sha256 equals the digest in its key AND in the user data, replays lib/init-host.sh.diff onto it (a context line holding {{TOKEN}} matches whatever value is rendered there; everything else must match literally), writes the candidate script and base64 user data to disk, and PRINTS the exact upload / create-launch-template-version / update-auto-scaling-group commands without running any of them. A human executes them, because whether the pinned version's AMI, IAM instance profile, security groups and subnets are still the right base is not visible to this tool and repointing would silently adopt them. It ends at the ASG repoint — no instance refresh, so running hosts are untouched and only newly launched hosts read the new script. Rollback is the same repoint back to the version pinned today; the old prefix stays addressable because the deployment is prune=False / retain_on_delete=True, and the uploaded object is deliberately left in place so a host that already launched on it keeps working. `verify` is automated and convergent: it asserts the AFTER-image (every placeholder-free added line present, every removed line absent) against the version the ASG PINS, never $Default, and never by replaying the diff.

ec2:EdgeLaunchTemplate new version pinning the new edge bundle prefix. A new LT version alone does NOT update the running ASG — it pins a specific version and only new instances use a new one. pull records the rollback anchor, so it runs before push.

fixes.summary: The edge could not retry an upstream at all, by construction: OpenResty forbids cosockets in the balancer phase, yet the retry path re-read Redis there, so a failed upstream surfaced to the client as 500 instead of 502. The retry now reads only the shared dictionary and fails closed. Reproduced on a real host with the full Lua stack; this is a pre-existing defect, not one introduced by this range.

GET /users/{id}/tenants and /users/{id}/summary returned 500 for every input and echoed an internal index name in the error, because they were missing the feature gate the rest of that service applies and queried an index that is not enabled in every deployment.

POST /recipient-key/disable and POST /create-image-snapshot performed their destructive action even when the request body was missing the parameters that action needs. Both now validate before acting. The other twelve collection-level write routes on that surface were checked and already behaved.

The network watchdog relaunched a microVM without reading the stop script's exit status. A failed stop can leave the previous Firecracker process alive, so relaunching gave one tenant two VMs. It now declines and prints a searchable pointer instead.

The edge read path follows the cluster reader endpoint, and the node ids the lag alarms use are now derived from the replication group's own id instead of its read endpoints. Because the reader parameter equals the primary when the switch is off, the lag alarms are only created when reading from a replica is actually enabled.

The launch path treats a tenant recorded as failed or requiring intervention as terminal for the current message: it marks the assignment done and stops redelivery instead of parking the message and holding the per-tenant ordering window until the deadline gate ends it. Capacity is still reclaimed by the health-check reaper, and the tenant is still recoverable through the public API.
A reconcile that could not read its desired state tore the existing egress chain down (fail-open). It now keeps the existing chain when the desired state is unavailable.

start and restart on a tenant already recorded as failed or requiring intervention now return 409 with a not-startable code and recovery guidance, at accept time and in the executor for the window where the status degrades after a 202, and a fail reason records why. Previously such a request was falsely accepted with a 202 and then occupied the head of that tenant's ordering group for the whole visibility window, blocking the tenant's only remaining exits.

install-edge.sh silently fell back to the Redis primary when it could not read the reader endpoint from SSM, and the only trace was a line in the install log, which no collector reads. Each box now emits a bounded custom metric so 'some boxes read the reader, some fell back' is visible off-host. The metric is a LOWER BOUND: if the cause is that the box cannot reach the network, the metric call fails the same way, so the alarm reads one way only — if it fires a box fell back, silence does not prove convergence. This REQUIRES the EdgeRole PutMetricData grant; without it every box writes a warning instead, the metric is permanently absent, the alarm never fires, and the result is indistinguishable from not having applied this at all.

params_changed.name: install-edge.sh per-AWS-CLI-call network budget
params_changed.old_default: AWS CLI defaults: 60s connect + 60s read, standard retry mode, 3 total attempts (~180s worst per call)
params_changed.new_default: AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS=1 as a command-level prefix, ~10s per call, plus a bounded 3-attempt outer retry with 2s backoff (~34s per call site)

Future hosts: a black-holed SSM or CloudWatch endpoint can no longer burn ~540s inside a 300s health_check_grace_period, so adding this observability can no longer get the box replaced by the ASG. The prefix is deliberately not exported, so the Fluent Bit S3 download later in the same script keeps the CLI's default retries.

fixes.summary: The suspend and rebuild execution budgets were below what stop-vm.sh can legitimately take, so the control plane could declare failure while SSM was still running and the VM ended up actually stopped with the operation recorded as failed. The budgets are now derived from the script's worst measured wall clock, and a self-heal FATAL is written to stderr as well so the reason reaches the caller.

params_changed.name: lifecycle suspend exec budget (stop-vm step)
params_changed.new_default: 50s (STOP_VM_WORST_SEC=46 plus 4s margin; 46 = 17s lock contention + 24s guest flush + 5s terminate)
params_changed.runtime_impact: running system: a suspend legitimately taking 31-50s is no longer recorded as failed while the VM is in fact stopped. The TOTAL deadline is unchanged, so the async-retry margin for suspend drops from 60s to 40s — a suspend needing more than one AWS-side retry now has less room. That is the trade-off, not a free win.

params_changed.name: lifecycle rebuild exec budget (rebuild-vm step)
params_changed.new_default: 66s (STOP_VM_WORST_SEC=46 plus an O(1) rename plus 20s launch headroom)
params_changed.runtime_impact: running system: same state-consistency fix as suspend. The rebuild async-retry margin drops from 60s to 24s within the same total deadline, so rebuild tolerates fewer AWS-side retries.

fixes.summary: The tenant-query preflight told the operator to fix something without naming the field it actually checks, so following the message still left the gate failing. The remediation text now names the field.
The retry-on-second-connect surface gained a discriminating probe, so a claimed fix cannot pass against a stand-in.

A fresh deployment could answer every route with 502: the Lambda stack injected only the deadline tiers the config file happened to spell out, while the function required all of them at import time, so a config omitting one tier killed the API before it served a request. Every tier is now derived from the shipped default table when config omits it, and the requirement is checked against what is actually injected.

params_changed.name: lambda:openclaw-api DEADLINE_SEC_<ACTION> env keys
params_changed.old_default: only the tiers present in config.yml lifecycle.deadline_sec were injected; a missing tier raised at import
params_changed.new_default: all eight lifecycle actions are injected, falling back to create_deadline.default_deadline_sec_for(action)
params_changed.runtime_impact: running system: an import-time raise that 502'd every route is removed. No tier value changes for a config that already listed all eight. Future hosts: unaffected, this is Lambda-only. Lambda: cold start no longer depends on config completeness.

fixes.summary: An egress allow entry's dport was silently coerced, so a non-integer value was accepted and written. It is now accepted only as a real integer.

WAF rate limiting is now expressed in the same units as the API Gateway limit so the two can be compared (a client's real ceiling is the lower of the two), and its audit log keeps only blocked requests with the API key redacted.

params_changed.name: waf.evaluation_window_sec
params_changed.old_default: not configurable; the effective window was 300s
params_changed.runtime_impact: no behaviour change at the default, since the effective window stays 300s. Setting another allowed value changes the per-IP ceiling, which is rate_limit_per_ip divided by this window.

params_changed.name: waf.logging_enabled
params_changed.new_default: true — BLOCK-only records to the log group named by waf.log_group_name
params_changed.runtime_impact: running system: enabling WAF now also starts writing CloudWatch Logs, a real recurring cost on a deployment with a high block rate. Only blocked requests are recorded and the API key is redacted. Set it to false if that cost is unwanted.

fixes.summary: The cosocket restriction in the balancer phase had only a unit-test stand-in, which a fake Redis module can satisfy while the real OpenResty phase still fails. A real-phase integration assertion now covers it.
The six host-egress routes that were already live now have their OpenAPI contract written down, so a typed client can be generated against them.

Numeric DynamoDB attributes were serialized as strings by the response wrapper, contradicting the integer type the OpenAPI document declares for those fields on GET /tenants/{id} and GET /hosts/rolling-jobs/{id}.

The edge read its Redis coordinates from systemd Environment= entries, but nginx strips what a worker inherits from its parent (keeping only TZ), so route.lua's os.getenv was always nil. Warmup then treated 'no coordinates' as 'nothing to probe' and marked the box ready, making the readiness gate permanently fail-open. Coordinates are now rendered into init_by_lua_block and delivered through a single channel, and a warmup with no coordinates fails closed.

A tenant's allowedOrigins is decided once, at deploy time, by an SSM parameter the applying operator cannot see or override, and the write is a WHOLE-ARRAY REPLACEMENT: the single value passed in becomes the only origin that tenant may connect from. Read this before relying on it — when that parameter is '*', the Origin check is effectively DISABLED for the whole fleet, and the previous code could not be told apart from a correct narrowing because all three outcomes were equally silent. All three now log distinctly, with the wildcard case logged as a warning rather than as success.

An exception raised while building the runtime report was reported over a channel that could not carry a non-Latin-1 message, so the caller saw a transport error instead of the real exception type and text, and the operator had nothing to search for. Reporting now goes through an ASCII-safe path that preserves both.

restore that blew its deadline landed in `status=failed` and stayed there: this function only admitted `suspended`, suspend only admits running/stopped, start/restart hit the #624 tombstone gate, and rebuild takes the wake path without RESTORE_KEY, i.e. an empty disk. The data was still in S3 (the deadline fence only SETs, it never REMOVEs `restore_backup_key`) but no ordinary API could get it back. Two things the dead attempt left behind also had to be cleared first, and neither had an owner: the still-held `restore_reservation_id` (the fence retains the token on purpose per #412, while the orphan-token reaper only scans `capacity_reservation_id`, the deadline executor does not release, and the reaper matrix only handles `status=restoring` — so it leaked permanently), and a VM nobody accounts for (launch succeeded, finalize's CAS lost to the fence, and the CCF branch released the reservation without stopping the VM). `failed` is now a controlled entry guarded by `suspended_at`, which is what distinguishes 'failed with no VM' from 'failed while a VM may still be running' — admitting the latter would start a second copy of the same tenant.

The 8081 allow rule could not be opened at all. Admission resolved a single SPIRE server IPv4 (from env, else one SSM parameter) and required the requested `dst` to equal exactly that /32. The control-plane Lambda has no VPC attachment, so it cannot resolve a private name, and the resolver returned None on any failure — fail-closed by design — which denied every 8081 request. Even when it did resolve, a multi-AZ VPC endpoint has one address per AZ, so a single /32 can never cover the SPIRE service. The special case is removed: 8081 now goes through the same guards as any other non-red-line port (red-line port set, IMDS refusal, minimum prefix, VPC_CIDR/TENANT_SUPERNET containment).

Two defects on `POST /hosts/egress` with `wait=true`, both in the same dispatch path. (a) An incomplete collection still answered 200 with ok=true. `_collect` only reports invocations that came back inside the window; a targeted host that never answered was neither counted as a failure nor back-filled, so `host_count` could be smaller than the number of targets while `ok` stayed true — and the rollback side already treated the same situation as a failure, so the two paths disagreed about the same fleet. The targeted path now computes the missing set, reports `expected_host_count` / `missing_hosts` / `collection_incomplete`, folds it into `ok`, and answers 207. `targets="all"` deliberately does NOT do this: its expected set is a DDB snapshot that can contain terminated or SSM-unmanaged hosts and can miss a just-registered host the tag fan-out will still hit, so a set difference there would manufacture a permanent 207 — it reports the count only. (b) `TimeoutSeconds=timeout + 10` could derive an illegal SSM parameter. SSM's minimum is 30 and boto rejects anything smaller at the parameter-validation layer, before the call leaves the process; `timeout` comes from `EGRESS_APPLY_TIMEOUT`, which an operator may set to any value, so any setting at or below 19 made every `POST /hosts/egress` return 502 — the endpoint was entirely unavailable, not merely degraded. Clamped at the dispatch site with `max(30, timeout + 10)`.

params_changed.name: SSM SendCommand TimeoutSeconds derived by _dispatch_apply for the egress chain
params_changed.old_default: timeout + 10, i.e. 100s at the shipped EGRESS_APPLY_TIMEOUT default of 90
params_changed.new_default: max(30, timeout + 10), i.e. still 100s at the shipped default of 90
params_changed.runtime_impact: On a default deployment nothing changes: EGRESS_APPLY_TIMEOUT defaults to 90, so both expressions yield 100. The clamp only bites when an operator lowers EGRESS_APPLY_TIMEOUT to 19 or less, where the old expression produced a value below SSM's minimum of 30 and boto refused the call — every POST /hosts/egress answered 502. After the clamp the same setting keeps a short collection budget (that is a legitimate operational choice) while the SSM delivery deadline stays legal, so the endpoint answers instead of failing. The clamp is at the dispatch site rather than inside _apply_timeout() on purpose: the two numbers mean different things — timeout is our own collection budget, whose real ceiling is the API Gateway 29s window, whereas TimeoutSeconds is the deadline after which SSM abandons delivery. Raising the collection budget to satisfy SSM would silently change how long the caller waits.

fixes.summary: The edge integration gate's `init_by_lua_block` placeholder check was flaky: the same nginx.conf was judged 3/4 (FAIL) and 4/4 (PASS) by different runs, so it could block an unrelated change at random and pass at random when it should have failed. Two independent causes, both removed. First, the check was `awk <window> | grep -qF`; under the script's `set -uo pipefail`, `grep -q` exits on its first match, awk's next write gets EPIPE and dies non-zero, pipefail then fails the whole pipeline and the `&&` never incremented the counter — so whether a placeholder was counted depended on the race between grep exiting and awk writing again. The count is now done inside a single awk process, with no pipe. Second, the block boundary was guessed from indentation (`/^    }/`), so any nested Lua table whose closing brace happened to sit at four spaces closed the window early and all later placeholders went uncounted; the boundary is now brace-pair counting. The logic is extracted into `count_hint_placeholders()` and locked by three self-proving arms plus a negative arm: repeatable across rounds, block-aware (placeholders outside the block count 0), nesting-proof, and genuinely red when a coordinate placeholder is actually removed.

# shellcheck disable=SC1090
. "$FN"
CONF=host-scripts/edge/nginx.conf
test -f "$CONF" || { echo "FAIL missing $CONF"; exit 1; }
rc=0
# root cause 1 — the pipe. `grep -q` exits on its first match, awk's next write gets EPIPE
# and dies non-zero, and pipefail then fails the whole pipeline so the counter never
# increments. The only durable fix is that no pipe exists at all.
if grep -qE 'grep[^|]*-q|\|' "$FN"; then
  echo 'FAIL the shipped counter still contains a pipe or a grep -q:'
  grep -nE 'grep[^|]*-q|\|' "$FN" | sed 's/^/    /'
  rc=1
else
  echo 'ok the counter is a single awk process — no pipe, so no EPIPE to mis-attribute'
fi
# root cause 2 — the boundary. Insert a balanced nested brace pair whose CLOSING line is
# indented exactly four spaces. The old /^    }/ boundary closes the window there and
# counts 0; brace-pair counting still counts 4.
W="$(mktemp -d)"
awk '{ print }
     !ins && index($0, "init_by_lua_block") { print "        local _probe = {"; print "    }"; ins = 1 }' \
    "$CONF" > "$W/nested.conf"
N_NESTED="$(count_hint_placeholders "$W/nested.conf")"
echo "nested four-space closing brace inside the block -> $N_NESTED/4 (want 4)"
[ "$N_NESTED" = "4" ] || { echo 'FAIL the boundary is still guessed from indentation'; rc=1; }
grep -q 'local _probe = {' "$W/nested.conf" || { echo 'FAIL the fixture was not built'; rc=1; }
[ "$rc" = "0" ] && echo 'PASS both #658 root causes are closed: no pipe, and the block '\
'boundary survives a nested four-space closing brace'
exit "$rc"
